TITLE: meta-sight
TAGLINE: A memory for your home, worn on your face.
INTRO: Glasses that remember where you left things. Ask "where are my keys?" and it answers with a place, a distance and how long ago it saw them. It also warns you when something is close, in front, to the side or behind.
F1_H: It maps the house as you walk
F1: A few frames at a time go into Meta's MapAnything, which turns them into 3D points measured in metres. The pieces are joined into one map of the house.
F2: An object finder looks for the things people lose: keys, wallet, phone, remote, water bottle, backpack. Each one it finds is pinned on the map with a photo and the time.
F3: Ask out loud. A language model reads the pins and replies: "Your keys were on the dining table, about four metres ahead, two minutes ago."
MAP_H: Is the map in the right place?
MAP_BODY: Tested on {{N_WALKS}} walks from the TUM RGB-D benchmark, a public set of videos where a motion-capture system recorded exactly where the camera went. Each bar is how far the map's idea of the camera path sits from the true path, on average. Shorter is better.
MAP_NOTE: Most of the gain came from two changes. The map now spots a place it has already seen and pulls itself back into line, and it is told what lens the camera has instead of guessing it. Average error went from {{MAP_MEAN_BEFORE}} cm to {{MAP_MEAN_NOW}} cm.
PATH_H: The same walks, seen from above
PATH_BODY: The grey line is where the camera really went. The coloured line is where the map thinks it went.
FIND_H: Does it find the small stuff?
FIND_BODY: Scored on {{N_PHOTOS}} public photos from LVIS, a dataset where people outlined every object by hand. The score runs from 0 to 1 and rewards finding the real items without raising false alarms. Longer is better.
FIND_NOTE: Before, a small detector looked at a low-resolution frame. Now a larger detector does the looking, a separate image model double-checks every find, and each corner of the frame gets a zoomed-in pass, which is what helped keys and wallets. Average score went from {{FIND_MEAN_BEFORE}} to {{FIND_MEAN_NOW}}.
HOW_BODY: The glasses only stream. The map, the finder and the answers run on a Mac at home.
DATA_BODY: TUM RGB-D benchmark (Technical University of Munich, CC BY 4.0). LVIS v1 (CC BY 4.0, images from COCO). MapAnything (Meta, Apache 2.0). YOLOE-26 (Ultralytics, AGPL-3.0). SigLIP 2 (Google, Apache 2.0). Every picture and number on this page comes from these public datasets.
FOOT: Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, 2026.
FLOW_LABEL: Glasses, then the phone app, then the home server
FLOW1: Ray-Ban Meta glasses send their camera feed and motion to the phone.
FLOW2: Built on Meta's Wearables Device Access Toolkit. It passes frames on and speaks the answers.
FLOW3: Builds the map, finds your things and writes the answers.
